title: Robot Repair Station: Helmet Diagnostics Console
description: The user operates a robot repair station where a damaged helmet sits on a diagnostic platform. The user must interact with a control panel to run diagnostic scans, rotate the helmet for inspection, toggle X-ray wireframe mode, adjust repair beam intensity, select damage zones, and initiate the repair sequence — all while the robot animates and reacts to each step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Robot Repair Station scene. Load robot.glb and DamagedHelmet.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the DamagedHelmet on a circular metallic platform (MeshStandardMaterial, metalness 0.9) at center stage, scaled to 2x. Position the robot to the left, playing its idle animation via AnimationMixer. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 7) looking at the helmet. Add an ambient light (intensity 0.3), a directional light simulating overhead station lighting, and a colored point light (the repair beam) that the user controls. Create an HTML overlay control panel with these interactions requiring parameter validation: (1) A 'Scan' button that triggers a vertical green line (a thin plane) sweeping across the helmet over 2 seconds, and makes the robot play a different animation clip if available. (2) A rotation slider (0-360 degrees) that rotates the helmet on its Y-axis, validated to numeric range. (3) A 'Wireframe Toggle' button that switches the helmet materials between solid and wireframe mode. (4) A 'Beam Intensity' slider (0.0 to 5.0, step 0.1) controlling the point light intensity, validated to float range, with the light color interpolating from blue at low to red at high. (5) A 'Select Damage Zone' dropdown with options Front, Left, Right, Back that repositions the point light to illuminate that side of the helmet, validated against allowed values. (6) A 'Repair' button only enabled after scan has been run and a damage zone selected — clicking it triggers a particle burst effect (50 small spheres emitting outward from the helmet then fading) and the robot plays a celebratory animation. Display a status log div that records each action with a timestamp. Render with tone mapping and antialiasing enabled. Use OrbitControls for additional camera freedom.
